Welcome to my website! I'm a senior at Carnegie Mellon University, pursuing a degree in Statistics and Machine Learning. My research interests lie at the intersection of causal inference, statistical genetics, and computational biology. I'm particularly focused on developing and applying causal methods to single-cell genomics data to better understand complex diseases like Alzheimer's. Currently, I'm working on evaluating causal differential expression methods using single-cell RNA-seq data from Alzheimer's disease patients, combining techniques from statistics, causal inference, and genomics. I'm passionate about using rigorous statistical methods to uncover biological mechanisms that can inform prevention and treatment strategies for diseases.
